Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Intro chain and buying roles — org chart + procurement next steps

Hi Lisa — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a couple asks so we keep momentum:

1) Recap (your ask / fit): FinCo wants to evaluate Redwood for inference of customer support models (real-time chat and batch re-ranking). Key constraints: 
   - latency target: 150ms p50 for chat use-case
   - data residency: US-only (no cross-border logs)
   - procurement timeline: target decision by end of May / procurement review week of May 22

2) Next steps for us:
   - Please share a simple org map or list of stakeholders (economic buyer, procurement, legal/security owners). Even a single-page PowerPoint or PDF is perfect.
   - Intro to procurement/legal/security contacts so we can send a focused security/compliance packet and a short pricing band.
   - We'll prep a 1-page TCO and a one-sheet on security posture (SOC2 scope, encryption, KMS options).

Action items: can you send the stakeholder list/org chart and the procurement contact? If it's easier, an intro-to thread works too (we can keep it tight).

Attaching: we don’t have your org chart yet — will wait for yours before sending the pricing band.

Availability: Aditya and I are available Thu 14:00–16:00 PT if you'd like a short follow-up with procurement on the calendar.

Thanks — looking forward.

--
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Priyom — great talking earlier. Attaching a very small org chart (PDF) — it's not perfect but will give you the sense of who owns what. See notes inline: 

Attachment: FinCo_org-chart_Q2.pdf (one-page org chart)

Quick context:
- Economic buyer: Rajesh Patel, CFO (cc'd to keep in the loop; he sits on the analytics & ops steering committee).
- Procurement: Nadia Gomez, Head of Procurement (n.gomez@finco.com) — primary reviewer for vendor terms and commercial commitments.
- Legal / Security review: Mark Li, Sr. Counsel (mark.li@finco.com). Mark usually wants a SOC2 + data flow diagram and a short summary of data residency controls.

Timeline: procurement is targeting the week of May 22 for vendor reviews. If you can get a concise security packet and a pricing band over by Monday May 18, that will help prioritize your review.

I'll intro you to Nadia and Mark now in a separate short thread (so they have context) — please keep the email short and include the packet + a suggested slot for May 23.

Thanks,

Priyom — quick internal note before you reply to Lisa's intro:

- High priority: prepare a 2-page security snapshot (SOC2 scope, encryption at rest + in transit, KMS options, data retention controls) and a one-page pricing band (3 tiers: pilot, production-1, production-2 with typical throughput assumptions).
- Prep a short paragraph describing fallback/SLAs and how we handle private deployments (VPC/on-prem) since they emphasized residency.
- Monica: please pull standard security artifacts we can include (SOC2 cover page, data flow diagram, and a short redaction policy).

Goal: get packet ready to send on Mon May 18 so procurement can review week of May 22. Priyom — put proposed May 23 10:00–10:30 PT for a call with Nadia & Mark in the reply. I'll be on standby if you want me to join for commercial questions.

Marissa
Director, Sales Ops | Redwood Inference

- We support US-only log residency and customer-managed KMS (HSM) integrations.
- For production deployments we typically recommend dedicated capacity for predictable latency and HIPAA-like controls; we can show concrete cost examples on the call.
